newsitem.title: UK: GrandMet sees good outlook for Burger King.
newsitem.headline: GrandMet sees good outlook for Burger King.

text.p: Britain's Grand Metropolitan Plc, battling with McDonald's Corp for market share, said on Monday the global outlook for its Burger King chain continued to be good.
"There is significant scope for increasing both average unit volumes and the number of outlets," the company said in its first-half earnings statement.
Separately, the company unveiled its plan to merge with Britain's Guinness Plc in a deal that would create a food and drinks giant with a market capitalisation of more than 20 billion stg.
GrandMet said Burger King posted an operating profit of 69 million stg, up four percent in local currency terms, for the first half ended March 31.
Worldwide same-store sales rose 2.7 percent, and U.S. comparable store sales grew 2.5 percent, although the U.S. trend slowed in the second quarter, GrandMet said.
"In the U.S., Burger King's market share increased again following three successive years of market growth," GrandMet said.
Burger King competes fiercely with McDonald's, which recently slashed some key sandwich prices in the U.S. as part of a plan to boost its sales.
GrandMet said Burger King's European businesses reported an operating loss in the first half, mainly due to closure costs for stores in Britain and Germany.
"The underlying trading performance (of the European business) therefore improved significantly on the second half of last year," GrandMet said.
GrandMet said a record 406 Burger King units were opened in the first half -- 30 percent above last year -- resulting in a total of 9,029 restaurants in 53 countries.
